question: Why is the South's average daily rate lower this summer than last summer? We didn't cut prices.
answer:
# Why the South's average daily rate fell: product mix, not price

The South's average daily rate fell from **€34.05 to €29.82 (−12.4%)**, but **every category's rate went up**. The drop comes entirely from renting a much higher share of cheap equipment and a lower share of expensive equipment.

## Every category got more expensive per day

| Category | Rate FY2026 | Rate FY2027 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| ACC Access | 53.68 | 55.92 | +4.2% |
| EAR Earthmoving | 103.36 | 107.35 | +3.9% |
| PWT Power tools | 14.55 | 15.15 | +4.1% |
| PWL Power and lighting | 29.26 | 30.49 | +4.2% |
| CON Concrete and compaction | 22.44 | 23.35 | +4.1% |

These increases fit the South's new list prices from 2026-04-06, which were in force for all of this summer's weeks. You're right: there was no price cut.

## The mix swung toward the cheapest category

| Category | Days FY2026 | Days FY2027 | Change | Share FY2026 | Share FY2027 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PWT (~€15/day) | 23,485 | 33,509 | **+43%** | 41.6% | **51.5%** |
| CON (~€23/day) | 10,110 | 11,700 | +16% | 17.9% | 18.0% |
| PWL (~€30/day) | 7,026 | 7,116 | +1% | 12.5% | 10.9% |
| ACC (~€55/day) | 9,782 | 8,291 | **−15%** | 17.3% | 12.7% |
| EAR (~€105/day) | 6,013 | 4,464 | **−26%** | 10.7% | 6.9% |

Power tools now account for over half of all on-rent days. Earthmoving, the highest-rate category, fell from about 1 in 9 days to about 1 in 14.

## Splitting the €4.23 drop

- **Mix effect:** If this summer's days had been charged at last summer's rates, the average would have been **€28.65**. That is **−€5.40** from the change in what was rented.
- **Rate effect:** The price increases added back **+€1.17**.
- **Net:** −€4.23, which matches the reported figures. Both summers' category data reconcile to the reported revenue within rounding, and no South weekly files are missing.

## What it means for the business

Total revenue rose only **1.0%** (€1.92m to €1.94m), while on-rent days rose **15.4%**. Volume growth came almost entirely from low-value power tool rentals. Meanwhile, demand for earthmoving and access equipment fell by about 3,000 days. That loss nearly offset the 10,000 extra power tool days in revenue terms.

The staff notes for the period don't explain the shift; none of them relate to South demand. The useful next question is **why earthmoving and access days fell**. Possible causes include a lost contractor account, a competitor, fleet availability, or a pause in local construction. A breakdown by depot and customer would show whether the drop is concentrated somewhere.
